html:
Ava, or Inwa, is a city on the Irrawaddy river near modern Mandalay that was the capital of Burmese kingdoms for much of the time from 1364 to 1842. The first Ava kingdom fought the Mon kingdom of Pegu in the Forty Years' War and fell to Shan raiders in 1527.

The map's snapshots from 1650 to 1715 show the restored Taungoo kingdom, which ruled from Ava again from 1635. King Thalun rebuilt the state after the wars of the 1500s and ordered a great survey of land and people in 1638. The kingdom was stable but slowly weakening. Horsemen from Manipur raided it from the 1720s, and in 1752 a Mon revolt from the south took Ava.

Alaungpaya then founded the Konbaung dynasty and reunited the country (Taungoo and Konbaung Burma). Ava was again a royal capital at times until 1842. Later history is under Burma.
